note: Every hymn found in the Faith Presbyterian bulletins posted online is now in Hark, from May 10, 2015 through November 15, 2026. Where the words are under copyright, the page shows the bulletin page as printed, with no typed words. A few hymns from the older bulletins have only a title for now, because those bulletins print no music or words.

The video frame now asks for picture in picture and full screen permission up front. Whether a phone floats the video when you press Home is up to Chrome and YouTube, so for a floating window you can tap Play on YouTube to open the recording in the YouTube app.

On a phone, the small player now stays on screen as a floating window when you scroll down past it, so the song keeps playing in view. Tap it to go back to the pinned player. Hark never pauses a song when you leave the screen.

On My Song Forever Shall Record, the two melodies are now at the top of the page, right under the play buttons and above the words. Melody 1 is WINCHESTER NEW and Melody 2 is MARYTON, and each has its own Play this melody button.

My Song Forever Shall Record is sung to two melodies, and its page now keeps them apart. The recordings are grouped as Melody 1, WINCHESTER NEW, from today's Trinity Hymnal, and Melody 2, MARYTON, from the 1961 blue Trinity Hymnal. Play song starts the hymnal melody, each group has its own Play this melody button, and the player names the melody that is playing.
My Song Forever Shall Record now shows both of its tunes, WINCHESTER NEW and MARYTON. Each recording names the tune sung that day, and the page has the music for WINCHESTER NEW.

My Song Forever Shall Record and May the Mind of Christ My Savior now start at the right place in the November 15 evening recording and stop by themselves. That evening Faith sang My Song Forever Shall Record to the tune MARYTON, from the 1961 (blue) Trinity Hymnal, and its page now says so.

On a phone, a Play song button now sits beside Play all at the top of a song, and the video plays there, above the words. Leave the page and it floats as a small player that keeps playing. Tap it to go back to the song.
Hark now uses cookies and Google Analytics to understand how people use it, and says so at the foot of the About page. It honors Global Privacy Control.
A song that is not in the Trinity Hymnal, such as Hail, Gladdening Light, no longer points to the hymnal. Its page names the bulletin it came from.
On a computer, the player now sits right above the words of the song that is playing. A button on the player bar lets it float in a corner instead.
Hail, Gladdening Light, a reader request, from the September 13 evening service. It is not in the Trinity Hymnal, so it has no hymn number.
Be Thou My Vision has a recording from the November 15 evening service. It stops by itself when the song ends.
Hark can count visits and listening time without a name or an address. It stays quiet when the browser asks not to be tracked.
Songs taken from a Faith Presbyterian bulletin now link to that bulletin.
Moving the pointer over the small player does not drag it. A click opens the song, and it follows only while the button is down.
Leave a song and a small player floats above the bar. Tap it to open that song, with the words under the video.
A song keeps playing while you move around Hark, and the player bar stays up. Where the device allows it, the song title can show with play, pause, and next.
Play all and Auto play all are on the song list, on a search, and on each song. Auto play all follows hymn number from wherever a song was started.
Play next song moves through the list. Auto play all keeps going through the book by number.
Play all is on the home page and the themes list. A new copy of Hark loads as soon as it is published.
Play all the songs in a season. Each recording stops when the song ends.
